name: Afghan Mujahideen
alt: Islamic Union of Mujahideen of Afghanistan

predecessors.name: Afghanistan
predecessors.text: the countryside outside the cities and roads held by the Soviets and the government: 'Almost 80 percent of the country was outside government control'

successors.name: Afghanistan
successors.text: the whole country, which the mujahideen coalition governed as the Islamic State of Afghanistan from 28 April 1992

capitals.name: Peshawar (Pakistan), seat of the Afghan Interim Government in exile

ledger.x: 1979: the Afghan mujahideen rise against the Soviet-backed government and the invading Soviets.
1979: guerrilla war against the government's cities and roads.
February 1989: the seven Sunni parties form the Afghan Interim Government.
February 1989: the government in exile sits at Peshawar, Pakistan (infobox headquarters) after 'the groups attempted to form a coalition government in exile from Peshawar'.
April 1992: the mujahideen win and become the Islamic State of Afghanistan (successor named on the page; Afghanistan page infobox 'Islamic State: 28 April 1992').

wars.name: Soviet–Afghan War
wars.outcome: Infobox result 'Afghan mujahideen victory', 25 December 1979 to 15 February 1989; the last Soviet column left on 15 February 1989.

wars.name: Battle of Jalalabad (1989)
wars.outcome: The government 'rallied to break the siege of Jalalabad' in March 1989, its first major victory in years; 'the mujahideen failed to win the 1989 Battle of Jalalabad' (Islamic Unity page).

wars.name: Afghan civil war (1989-1992)
wars.outcome: The Afghan government lost the countryside, Najibullah resigned on 14 April 1992 and Kabul fell on 28 April 1992; the Islamic State of Afghanistan followed.

certainty.note: The rebels held the countryside around Soviet and government cities and roads; no page gives a line, only shares ('almost 80 percent', 'only 10 percent' for the government in 1991).
